definition: To limit the rate at which a function is invoked, ensuring it only runs after a specified period of inactivity to avoid excessive calls.
example: We debounce the input event handler to prevent sending an API request on every keystroke, triggering it only after the user stops typing for 300ms.

definition: An operation is idempotent if executing it multiple times has the same effect as executing it once, ensuring no additional side effects occur on repeated calls.
example: Sending multiple identical HTTP PUT requests to update a user profile is idempotent because the resource state remains consistent regardless of the number of repeated requests.

definition: The amount of work or data processed by a system in a given amount of time, often used to measure system performance or capacity.
example: Increasing the database throughput allowed the application to handle more user requests per second without slowing down.

definition: A design pattern used in software to detect failures and encapsulate the logic of preventing a failure from constantly recurring, typically by stopping requests to a failing service for a period of time.
example: In a microservices architecture, a circuit breaker can stop calls to a service that's down to avoid overwhelming it and allow time for recovery.
